items.prompt:
Early life added which gas to the atmosphere?
A) Oxygen
B) Helium
C) Neon
D) Gold vapor

steps: Early life added oxygen to the air.

items.prompt:
Early organisms added oxygen to the air through
A) photosynthesis
B) burning
C) erosion
D) freezing

The oxygen-rich atmosphere allowed
A) new oxygen-using life to evolve
B) all life to disappear
C) no change
D) the Sun to dim
items.answer: A) new oxygen-using life to evolve

items.prompt:
Did Earth's atmosphere always have lots of oxygen?
A) No, it built up over time from life
B) Yes, always
C) It never had oxygen
D) Oxygen came from the Moon
items.answer: A) No, it built up over time from life

items.prompt:
A way living things affect the atmosphere today is that plants
A) take in carbon dioxide and add oxygen
B) make the Sun brighter
C) stop the wind
D) create rocks
items.answer: A) take in carbon dioxide and add oxygen

items.prompt:
Life and Earth's systems have
A) influenced each other over time
B) never interacted
C) stayed exactly the same
D) nothing to do with each other
items.answer: A) influenced each other over time

items.prompt:
The rise of oxygen shows life and Earth changed together because
A) life made oxygen that changed the air, and the new air then allowed new life
B) oxygen came from space
C) life never affected the air
D) the air never changed
items.answer: A) life made oxygen that changed the air, and the new air then allowed new life

items.prompt:
The best argument that life and Earth changed together is that
A) early life made oxygen, changing the atmosphere, which then allowed new life to evolve
B) nothing ever changed
C) only Earth changed
D) only life changed
items.answer: A) early life made oxygen, changing the atmosphere, which then allowed new life to evolve

steps: Life and Earth influenced each other.
